Thanks for looping us in. Quick context from our side: Acme is switching to usage-based billing for our enterprise customers in November and we need the Marketplace path to handle per-customer SKU mapping, seller-settlement reconciliation, and invoice downstreaming to our accounting system.

Two questions up front:
- Can Redwood's fulfillment webhook include both the marketplace SKU ARN and a customer_id dimension so our ERP can reconcile?
- Is there a signing/shared-secret mechanism we can use for the webhook so we don't need to expose a public endpoint unauthenticated?

I've attached our current entitlement matrix and a sample of the invoice format we consume. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through.

Alyssa

Thanks Alyssa — good requirements. Short answers first: yes on the SKU ARN and customer_id dimensions; yes on webhook signing. Longer details and proposed plan below.

Plan (summary):
1) Entitlement mapping: we'll add a per-transaction metadata bundle on the fulfillment event that includes marketplace_sku_arn, seller_id, and customer_external_id. We recommend you include your internal customer_id in the Marketplace "customId" field at activation time to keep the mapping stable.
2) Webhook signing: Redwood will sign outgoing fulfillment webhooks with an HMAC-SHA256 signature in an "X-RI-Signature" header. We will provide a key rotate endpoint and a shared-secret per-environment (sandbox/prod).
3) Invoice routing: we can emit an "invoice-ready" event to your accounting webhook with the aggregated usage + invoice_id. We'll also attach a downloadable CSV link behind a signed, short-lived URL.

Action items for Acme: share a sample activation payload (if different from the entitlements sheet) and confirm desired sandbox webhook URL. For Redwood: we'll prepare a dev sandbox with signed webhooks and a mapping guide by Friday.

I'll attach a draft webhook example and a quick SOW outline.

-Irene
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Looping in from the Marketplace side. A couple of constraints to surface:
- Marketplace activation events include the AWS-specified BuyerId and Entitlement fields; sellers should not rely on Marketplace changing those field names. We recommend storing both the Marketplace BuyerId and your own customer_external_id to avoid reconciliation drift.
- For seller-led metering, make sure your metering service reports the usageDimension exactly as published in the listing; mismatch is the most common cause of failed settlement.

If helpful, I can provision a test seller account in the AWS Partner Sandbox and create a fake buyer account for validation.

-Ravi
AWS Partner Solutions

Great — I've sketched a technical checklist for our eng + ops teams (pasted below). Please confirm anything missing from Acme.

Technical checklist:
- Sandbox: provision Marketplace test seller & buyer (Ravi)
- SKU mapping: map listing SKU -> internal product_code -> Acme.customer_id (infra task)
- Metering reporter: ensure usageDimension string matches listing; support batched reporting for hourly aggregation
- Webhook: HMAC-SHA256 signing, timestamp header, replay protection (nonce + TTL)
- Fallbacks: if webhook fails 5x, write event to durable queue and send email to Acme ops + Redwood billing team
- Invoice export: single CSV per billing window with column parity to Acme ERP sample (attached)
- Key rotation: endpoint + 30d expiry default for sandbox keys

Target timeline: sandbox ready by Fri (2028-08-25), pilot activation with 3 buyers week of 2028-09-04, full rollout mid-September.

Kimberly

2) For invoice exports, we prefer zero decimal rounding in cents to avoid ERP import issues (we can provide CSV import template).
